transcript.text: This is Swift, an automated flood assistant working with local emergency services. Am I speaking with someone at 308 Stoney Fork Drive?
Yes, this is 308 Stoney Fork Drive. I’m here with two people, no water inside, and I can help—emergency services can send a truck.
Thank you for confirming your address and availability. How many people are at the home right now, including anyone who can't come to the phone?
There are two people here, and neither of them can’t come to the phone.

I heard you, thank you for sharing that. Is there anyone there who can't leave on their own, for example someone who uses a wheelchair, needs oxygen, or is bedbound? If it's a wheelchair, does it have a motor?
No one here can’t leave on their own. I just corrected myself — there are two people, and neither uses a wheelchair, needs oxygen, or is bedbound.
Understood, no one here can’t leave on their own. Is there water inside the home right now?

No, there’s no water inside the home right now.  
*(corrects themselves)*  
Actually, there is no water inside — I meant to say, no water inside.
Got it, no water inside the home right now. If neighbors need a ride out, do you have a high-clearance truck, a boat, or free seats in a vehicle?
I don’t have a boat, but I do have a high-clearance truck available. I’m not sure if I have any free seats right now — I’ll check.
Thanks for checking on seats and truck availability. Let me read that back: 2 people; no water inside yet; you can help with a truck. Is that right?

Yes, that’s right — two people, no water inside, and I can help with a truck.  
*(corrects themselves)*  
Actually, I can help with a truck, but no seats are available.

Got it — two people, no water, truck available, no seats. I've recorded that you may be able to help neighbors. A dispatcher may contact you. Only go out if it's safe for you, and never drive into water you can't see the bottom of. Goodbye.
